title: Sandbar Platform relevance sprint - hosted embeddings + reranker walkthrough
summary: Intro demo of Redwood hosted embeddings endpoint + reranking pipeline. Covered API shapes, console demo, tradeoffs (latency vs cost), caching and batching, security (VPC/KMS/SOC2), and pilot proposal. Customer interested in a 4-week pilot to validate relevance on product search with ~10M docs.
topics: Reranker endpoint and client side mixing
Latency vs cost tradeoffs and batching
Security: VPC/private deployments, KMS, audit logs
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-06-03 15:00 UTC | Duration: 42m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Ruiz (Sandbar Head of Search), Priya Menon (Sandbar ML), Liam O'Connor (Sandbar Infra)

[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Alex from Redwood, I'll run through a short hosted API demo for embeddings + rerank. Maya is on to show the console and some Optimize suggestions.
[00:15] Jordan Ruiz: Great thanks, we've got about 40 mins. High level we want to see how you handle product search relevance, especially with personalization and a big catalog. Our goal is faster time-to-relevance than building our own infra.
[00:30] Maya Patel: Awesome — quick agenda: API shapes for embeddings, how rerank endpoint works (server-side vs client-side), console walkthrough for tuning and Optimize suggestions, security notes, and then next steps for a pilot.
[01:05] Priya Menon: Quick note, our current stack: vector DB is - we use FossilVec (internal), some FAISS sharding, and an in-house lightweight re-ranker. Latency SLO is 120ms p95 for SERP first page, budget is tight.
[01:35] Alex Chen: Cool. First thing — hosted embeddings endpoint. You send up a document batch, we return numeric vectors. Example API call: POST /v1/embeddings with model=redwood-embed-2, input=[...]. Response is vectors plus tokenization debug if you enable.
[02:10] Liam O'Connor: How big are the vectors? Are there quantized variants? We care about memory in the vector DB.
[02:20] Maya Patel: By default 768 dims for the model I demo. We also have smaller 256-d variants and quantized float16 / int8 exports that reduce storage. On the console Optimize tab we show recommended quantization profiles per workload. A note, the embed endpoint supports batching up to 512 inputs per request with automatic size-based splitting.
[03:05] Jordan Ruiz: What about throughput and cost — batching helps but hurts latency. What's Redwood's guidance?
[03:15] Alex Chen: Right, tradeoff. For high QPS with less strict latency you can push larger batch sizes. For product search with tight p95 SLOs, we recommend smaller batch sizes and prefix/KV cache for repeated contexts. Maya will show cache hit metrics in the console.
[03:50] Maya Patel: Showing console now — live demo (screen share). Home -> Models -> Embed models. Here's an example workload profile we uploaded: 60% short queries, 40% long descriptions. Optimize flagged: use 256-d model for metadata-only embeddings and reserved capacity if monthly QPS exceeds 5M to lower unit cost.
[04:30] Priya Menon: Is there a per-vector cost we can estimate? We have 10M product vectors, we need a ballpark monthly.
[04:45] Alex Chen: We'll send detailed pricing but ballpark: hosted embedding requests priced per 1K vectors; storage/DB cost depends on your vector DB. For using Redwood-hosted vector store (optional), we have a combined price. We'll include spreadsheet.
[05:20] Jordan Ruiz: Reranking — show how it integrates with our current two-stage retrieval. We want to keep our ANN nearest neighbor step and then call a reranker to reorder top K.
[05:35] Maya Patel: Exactly, typical pattern: 1) ANN returns top 100, 2) call Redwood reranker endpoint with those candidates and query, 3) we return top 10. Our hosted rerank endpoint accepts candidate metadata + embeddings or raw text. It can also accept precomputed candidate embeddings to reduce compute.
[06:05] Alex Chen: Demo API shape: POST /v1/rerank with {query, candidates: [{id, score, embedding? ,payload?}], model: rerank-v1, strategy: hybrid}. Response includes score and explain tokens if you enable verbose.
[06:40] Priya Menon: Do you run the rerank model on GPU? What's p95 for rerank of 100 candidates?
[06:50] Maya Patel: For a 100-candidate rerank, p95 is around 90-130ms on our shared hosted fleet depending on model size; with Dedicated/reserved capacity we target sub-80ms. We also have a cheaper small reranker optimized for reranking at scale with quantized kernels.
[07:20] Liam O'Connor: For compliance — we need SOC2, KMS integration for encryption keys, and VPC peering. How do hosted and private differ?
[07:35] Alex Chen: Hosted supports customer-managed KMS for key wrapping and audit logs. For full VPC/private plane, Redwood Private is offered; it includes a control plane you own and optional on-prem images. SOC2 is available; we'll share the security deck.
[08:05] Jordan Ruiz: Can we do a hybrid? Like host embeddings in your hosted infra but keep keys on our KMS?
[08:12] Maya Patel: Yes, hybrid patterns are common — hosted inference with customer-managed KMS, and if you need network isolation we can do VPC peering or Dedicated pools.
[08:40] Alex Chen: Now quick deep dive on rerank scoring: our reranker combines semantic similarity, learned interaction features, and a learn-to-rank head. You can pass custom features per candidate (CTR, recency). We also support per-tenant fine-tuning or post-training calibration.
[09:15] Priya Menon: Fine-tuning — do you allow us to bring labeled data? What's the process?
[09:25] Maya Patel: Yes, you provide the labeled pairs and we can run a fine-tune or you can run training in your infra with our model weights in Private. For hosted, most customers prefer calibration and logistic blending because full fine-tune on hosted models has governance controls.
[09:55] Jordan Ruiz: Show me an example of a rerank payload with features.
[10:05] Maya Patel: Sure — candidates array with fields: id, text_snippet, embedding (optional), features:{click_rate, fresh_days}. If you have precomputed embeddings we skip text encoding and go straight to interaction model which lowers latency.
[10:40] Liam O'Connor: What about fallback policies? If the rerank model is unavailable do you auto-fall back to candidate score?
[10:50] Alex Chen: Yes, smart routing and fallback — you can configure per-route fallback to a simpler scoring function or older model. Redwood Console has rollout controls for canary and percentage-based traffic shifting.
[11:25] Maya Patel: Walking through Optimize — we uploaded token distribution and request latency traces. Optimize suggests reducing context window for your most common queries and enabling prefix caching for product pages which are repetitive. It also suggests a quantization profile for reranker when throughput spikes.
[12:10] Jordan Ruiz: For our pilot we want to validate end-to-end: 1) embeddings quality for our taxonomy, 2) rerank improves top-10 NDCG, 3) latency under 120ms p95 on our infra with Redwood hosted rerank. Is that doable?
[12:30] Alex Chen: Yes, typical pilot: 4 weeks, we run a shadow test against live traffic with sampling, run offline evals on your test set for NDCG/AUC and then a staging rollout. We'll produce a pilot report.
[12:55] Priya Menon: How do we ingest 10M docs for the pilot? Bulk upload or streaming?
[13:05] Maya Patel: Both. For bulk we have a /bulk/embeddings CSV ingest with resumable upload; streaming via API is for incremental. If you prefer, Redwood can assist with an initial ingest.
[13:35] Liam O'Connor: Network and egress — if data stays in-hosted Redwood, are there egress costs to our cloud?
[13:45] Alex Chen: Egress depends on deployment: if using private VPC or Dedicated in your region, egress is minimal. If using cross-region hosted, there may be standard cloud egress costs. We'll map this in the pilot proposal.
[14:10] Jordan Ruiz: Any limitations on candidate count for rerank? We typically want to rerank 200 top candidates in worst-case.
[14:20] Maya Patel: We support up to 500 candidates for rerank but recommend 50-200 typical. Larger candidate sets increase latency linearly; you can trade off by doing two-stage rerank: coarse then fine.
[15:00] Alex Chen: Quick aside, common mis-transcription / internal note: KV cache often shows up as KV cash in some transcripts, ignore.
[15:12] Jordan Ruiz: (laughs) noted.
[15:20] Maya Patel: Now showing a live curl example: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank -d '{"query": "waterproof hiking shoes", "candidates": [...], "model":"rerank-v1" }' Response shows scores and optional position deltas.
[15:48] Priya Menon: For debugging relevance regressions, do you offer eval sets and automated regression alerts?
[15:55] Maya Patel: Yes, Redwood Optimize supports eval suites — you upload labeled prompt-candidate pairs and we run daily evals. Alerts can trigger when NDCG drops beyond a threshold. This is a big differentiation for many customers.
[16:30] Alex Chen: Let's talk infra options for production: Hosted API (fastest) -> Dedicated reserved capacity -> Private (VPC or on-prem). Each step increases isolation and reduces variance in latency.
[16:55] Liam O'Connor: For Dedicated, how do autoscaling and burst capacity work? We expect seasonal spikes.
[17:05] Maya Patel: Dedicated pools can be configured with autoscaling policies and burst credits. You can set min/max GPU count and rules by queue length or token backlog. Bursts are billed but help keep SLOs during spikes.
[17:40] Jordan Ruiz: Security again — can we get IP allowlisting and SAML SSO for console?
[17:50] Alex Chen: Yes: IP allowlist, SAML/Sso with SCIM provisioning, RBAC roles. We include audit logs for each inference call for compliance.
[18:10] Priya Menon: Performance testing — can you run a benchmark with our sample queries and our cloud region?
[18:20] Maya Patel: We can. For pilots we offer a benchmark run where we replay sampled traffic against a dedicated pool and produce latency/cost estimates. We'll need a test key and sample traffic.
[18:45] Jordan Ruiz: Ok show me cost-control levers again in the console — caching, batching, model size — and how they map to dollar impact.
[18:55] Maya Patel: On the console cost breakdown we show per-token and per-request cost per route. For embeddings it's per vector, for rerank it's per candidate scored. Optimize simulates changing batch size or model and projects cost and p95 impact.
[19:30] Alex Chen: Quick live example of reranker compression: enabling quantized rerank-v1-small drops per-request cost by ~40% at the expense of mild accuracy loss (we show expected delta in NDCG).
[20:05] Priya Menon: We might try a split test where 10% traffic uses full model and 90% uses small quantized model during peak. Is that supported?
[20:15] Maya Patel: Yes, canary & rollout supports percentage-based traffic splits and automatic rollback on metric degradation.
[20:40] Jordan Ruiz: What logging / observability do we get per-request? We need token-level cost, latency histograms, and per-route error breakdowns.
[20:50] Alex Chen: The Console provides token-level cost, latency by model and route, error types, and tracing hooks that integrate with your observability stack. We can add trace ids to requests so you can correlate logs.
[21:25] Liam O'Connor: On data retention — do you retain inputs for longer than needed? We need a retention policy for PII.
[21:35] Maya Patel: Hosted has configurable retention. You can opt-out of data logging, set retention windows, and choose to have PII scrubbed. For strict requirements we recommend Private.
[22:00] Jordan Ruiz: OK let's role-play the pilot timeline and success metrics — what are realistic deliverables in 4 weeks?
[22:10] Alex Chen: Week 1: ingest sample corpus and run offline evals; Week 2: shadow traffic + metric collection; Week 3: tuning and Optimize recommendations; Week 4: staging rollout and pilot report with NDCG/latency/cost numbers. Deliverables: pilot report, tuning recipe, recommended deployment mode.
[22:45] Priya Menon: Any pre-reqs from our side? Access, sample data size, and legal.
[22:55] Alex Chen: We need a contact for infra (Liam), an eval set (Priya), and an NDA signed — we'll attach SOW and security docs. Also need sample traffic for the benchmark.
[23:20] Jordan Ruiz: What about model explainability — can we get tokens that influenced the rerank score?
[23:30] Maya Patel: We provide optional explain outputs (top contributing tokens and attention highlights) but they add latency; recommended for offline analysis.
[23:55] Alex Chen: Quick Q/A — Jordan: How do we handle synonyms and SKU matching?
[24:05] Maya Patel: Use hybrid reranking: pass exact-match features (SKU match flag) plus semantic embedding similarity. You can also add rule-based boosts pre-rerank.
[24:30] Priya Menon: Are there rate limits? We have spikes to 20k qps occasionally.
[24:40] Alex Chen: Hosted has default rate limits per account; for pilot we'd set higher and for production you'd move to Dedicated with committed throughput. For extreme QPS we support sharded inference pools.
[25:10] Liam O'Connor: For the embedding ingestion — can we stream updates to product catalog and have incremental re-embedding?
[25:20] Maya Patel: Yes, incremental updates supported. You can call embeddings API for changed docs and use upsert semantics if using Redwood vector store, or push to your vector DB if hosting.
[25:50] Jordan Ruiz: Any concerns about hallucination in reranker? We rely on product data and don't want invented items.
[26:00] Maya Patel: The reranker is tuned to prioritize candidate evidence and payload fields; hallucination is more of a concern for generative rerankers — we default to evidence-based scoring for product search. You can disable generation tokens in response.
[26:35] Alex Chen: Let's capture next steps and action items — I'm noting these as we speak.
[26:45] Jordan Ruiz: Quick question on model version pinning — if you pin to rerank-v1.3, do you get fixes?
[26:55] Maya Patel: Pinning means you won't automatically pick up new minor versions; we recommend staged rollouts for updates. Console supports per-route model pinning.
[27:20] Priya Menon: Can we get a small sandbox account to test?
[27:25] Alex Chen: Yes, we can enable a trial account with credits and sample data preloaded.
[27:40] Maya Patel: Also will share a sample script to run offline NDCG evals and a Postman collection.
[27:55] Jordan Ruiz: How will Redwood measure improvement — do you report delta NDCG and click-through uplift?
[28:05] Alex Chen: Pilot report will contain offline NDCG, A/B uplift estimates from shadow traffic, and latency/cost numbers.
[28:30] Liam O'Connor: For billing, do you have a pilot pricing structure?
[28:40] Alex Chen: We'll propose a pilot SOW with capped engineering hours and usage credits. After pilot, options: pay-as-you-go hosted or reserved Dedicated contract.
[29:05] Priya Menon: Ok we're ready to start the pilot but need the security docs first.
[29:15] Maya Patel: We'll attach SOC2, architecture diagram, and KMS integration guide.
[29:45] Alex Chen: Walk-through wrap up: main benefits recap — faster onboarding, Optimize suggestions to reduce cost, and production-grade fallbacks.
[30:05] Jordan Ruiz: A couple of last minute clarifications: we need sample rate-limit numbers, and can you provide a realistic per-10k candidate cost estimate?
[30:20] Alex Chen: We'll include per-10k-candidates and per-vector cost examples in the pricing spreadsheet.
[30:40] Priya Menon: Anything else on observability? We need SLI export to Datadog.
[30:50] Maya Patel: We integrate with Datadog/Prometheus via tracing hooks and export. We'll share integration docs.
[31:10] Jordan Ruiz: Great. Let's go over action items now.
[31:20] Alex Chen: I'll read them out.
[31:25] Maya Patel: Action items (captured):
[31:30] Alex Chen: 1) Alex - Send pilot SOW + pricing spreadsheet + security deck (Due: 2027-06-07).
[31:40] Jordan Ruiz: 2) Priya - Share eval set (10k labeled queries) and sample traffic (anonymized) (Due: 2027-06-06).
[31:50] Alex Chen: 3) Liam - Provide network contact and preferred region for Dedicated/peering (Due: 2027-06-05).
[31:58] Maya Patel: 4) Maya - Provision trial account and Postman collection, sample scripts (Due: 2027-06-04).
[32:10] Priya Menon: 5) Jordan - internally approve SOW and sign NDA (Due: 2027-06-08).
[32:20] Alex Chen: We'll also schedule a 30-min kickoff next Tuesday once NDA is done.
[32:30] Jordan Ruiz: Sounds good. Any other competitors you should know we evaluated? We looked at OpenVector and AtlasSearch.
[32:40] Alex Chen: Noted. We also sometimes see customers use Pinecone, Weaviate, and OpenAI for embeddings.
[32:55] Priya Menon: One last technical question — how deterministic are embeddings across model restarts? We need stable vectors for incremental indexing.
[33:05] Maya Patel: Embeddings are deterministic per model version given same tokenizer and parameters. If you change quantization or model version there will be drift; Optimize flags suggested reindex windows.
[33:30] Liam O'Connor: Ok that's great. Quick recap of the pilot success metrics: +NDCG delta > 0.08, p95 latency < 120ms, and cost per query within budget.
[33:45] Alex Chen: We'll include those in the SOW.
[33:55] Jordan Ruiz: Anything else?
[34:00] Maya Patel: I'll attach demo artifacts: the Postman collection link, console screenshots, and a lightweight benchmarking script.
[34:15] Priya Menon: Thanks everyone, that was helpful.
[34:20] Alex Chen: Thanks, appreciate your time. We'll follow up with the SOW and security docs.
[34:28] Jordan Ruiz: End of call.
